extracted.intended_audience: NIH extramural research community (investigators, applicants, research administrators, small businesses)
extracted.subtask_description: A news/index page summarizing recent NIH extramural policy updates, resources, and tips relevant to preparing and submitting NIH grant applications and managing awards. Items include announcements about application formats, data management plans, reproducibility expectations, and peer review changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selecting appropriate research models (New Approach Methodologies — NAMs)
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH supports a wide range of scientifically sound approaches to advance understanding of human health and disease. Investigators should still select the models most appropriate for their specific research questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encouraged to choose models that enhance human relevance and translational potential while ensuring scientific soundness; select model(s) tailored to the specific research question rather than adopting approaches solely because they are encouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: PF5 Collaborative International Research Projects — follow application format
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH released a 6-minute overview video of the new Collaborative International Research Project (PF5) award structure to explain key features and application format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should watch the overview to learn the PF5 application format and how applications may be split into linked awards after review and before Just-in-Time requests; prepare applications consistent with the PF5 format requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the 2026 Pilot Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plan format
rubrics_metrics.description: A new 2026 Pilot DMS Plan format is available, based on a simplified set of required elements to use when preparing Data Management and Sharing Plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing DMS Plans for applicable submissions, adopt the 2026 pilot format and include the simplified required elements specified by NIH.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embed replication and reproducibility throughout NIH research
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH emphasizes that the reliability of biomedical research is foundational; the Gold Standard Science plan advances a commitment to replication and reproducibility and NIH launched a Replication and Reproducibility Initiative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should incorporate replication and reproducibility considerations into applications and award activities (design, methods, analysis, documentation) and be aware of NIH efforts to incentivize and institutionalize replication efforts and new highlighted topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: "Competitive but not discussed" review designation (under emergency modifications)
rubrics_metrics.description: Following emergency modifications to review processes, the middle third of applications in a study section were designated as 'competitive but not discussed' to recognize that strong applications may fall below a 33% cut off.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants who receive this designation should understand it signifies competitiveness without discussion in that review round; be aware of how these procedural changes affect review outcomes and next steps (e.g., resubmission or administrative actions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Awareness of centralized peer review (CSR consolidation)
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH centralized peer review within the Center for Scientific Review (CSR) to strengthen efficiency, competition, and transparency; the page summarizes initial effects after one year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants and administrators should be aware that peer review processes are centralized at CSR and consider potential impacts on study section assignment, review timelines, and competitiveness when preparing submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subscribe to NIH Extramural Nexus and use NIH resources to stay informed
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH Extramural Nexus is presented as a source for the latest updates on grants policies, processes, and resources. The page invites readers to subscribe to Nexus emails to stay informed about updates, policy changes, and resources affecting the NIH extramural research community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regularly monitor Nexus announcements, subscribe to email updates, and review linked resources (videos, guide notices, formats) to ensure applications and plans comply with current NIH requirements and guidance.
